question.text: An Automatic Conversion Clause in a hybrid security:

answer.text: Gives the investor an option to convert at any time of their choosing
Automatically converts equity back into debt if the company misses targets
Mandates compulsory conversion of convertible debt or preference shares into equity on occurrence of a pre-defined trigger (e.g., IPO, revenue milestone)
Requires 75% shareholder approval for every conversion event

explanation.text: The Logic: Per the AIF Managers workbook on conversion clauses (pp. 297-298), an Automatic Conversion Clause requires convertible debt securities or convertible preference shares to compulsorily convert into equity on the occurrence of a pre-defined trigger event, such as achievement of a revenue milestone, a Pre-Series A capital raise, or an Initial Public Offering. Optional conversion, by contrast, is the investor's right but not an obligation. The Trap: Option A describes optional conversion, where the investor chooses if and when to convert. Option B inverts the mechanism by suggesting equity reverts to debt, which is not what an Automatic Conversion Clause does. Option D invents a shareholder-approval gate that is not part of the source description of automatic conversion. Note: The defining feature of automatic conversion under pp. 297-298 is the pre-defined trigger that compels conversion, in contrast to optional conversion where the investor retains discretion.
